question: Which statement best captures how the web changes the true-fan arithmetic in Kelly's account?
options: Aggregators pay creators higher shares, so a few hundred fans suffice
Creators keep the full payment and niche fans become findable
Cheaper purchases mean a fan no longer needs to spend a day's wages
Crowdfunding platforms ensure any project reaches its funding goal

private.explanation: Two separate effects combine: keeping the full price (reduces fans needed) and long-tail reachability (makes the fans findable). The other options invent guarantees the essay does not make.
option_explanations: Aggregators are described as beneficiaries, not payers of higher shares.
Right: directness lowers the fans needed, and the tail makes the niche audience findable.
The one-day-wage assumption stays; the web changes who keeps the money and who can find whom.
Kelly says campaign success depends on what you ask of fans.
